Job Description: The Planning Team Leader for Guardian Wealth Partners (GWP) is a strategic leadership role responsible for building, leading, and scaling a high-performing advisor team within Guardian’s fee-based Registered Investment Advisor platform. In addition to overseeing the GWP Planning team and client delivery, this leader will play a critical role in developing and executing the client acquisition go-to-market strategy for Guardian Wealth Partners, including target client segments, referral pathways, distribution partnerships, and scalable engagement models. This individual will own the end-to-end acquisition, growth and retention strategy for prospects and clients originating from other Guardian business lines, with accountability for converting qualified opportunities into long-term advisory relationships, delivering differentiated client experience, and building servicing models that support retention, and deeper engagement. The role will partner closely with Group Distribution and other enterprise stakeholders to build the Guardian Wealth Partners practice, strengthen connectivity across business lines, and ensure the offering is positioned as a compelling wealth management solution for clients across different targeted segmentations ranging from mass affluent to high net worth through a combination of fully digital and hybrid engagement models. Key Responsibilities Sales & Growth Leadership Lead and develop a team of (centralized/in-house) advisors responsible for converting inbound leads into long‑term advisory relationships. Define and execute the client acquisition go-to-market strategy for Guardian Wealth Partners, including client segmentation, channel prioritization, referral source development, advisor coverage models, and conversion strategies. Develop segmented servicing models that align client needs, complexity, and relationship value with the appropriate combination of digital, hybrid, and advisor-led engagement. Drive growth across subscription‑based planning, fee‑based financial planning, and fee‑based investment management offerings. Build the operating rhythm, metrics, and feedback loops needed to evaluate go-to-market effectiveness, including lead quality, conversion rates, advisor productivity, client acquisition cost, revenue growth, and client outcomes. Serve as a strategic partner to senior leaders across Distribution, Wealth Management, Product, Marketing, Operations, and Compliance to support the continued growth and maturation of the Guardian Wealth Partners practice. Client Journey & Experience Design and oversee the servicing and retention strategy for Guardian Wealth Partners clients, ensuring clients receive consistent, high-quality experience from initial engagement through onboarding, planning, implementation, and ongoing relationship management. Ensure a consistent experience across digital planning tools, fully digital workflows, and hybrid advisor‑led engagements. Champion a client‑centric, education‑driven approach that builds trust, clarity, and long‑term partnerships with clients. Ensure advice delivery is aligned with fiduciary standards and the firm’s holistic planning philosophy. Establish proactive client engagement standards, including ongoing planning reviews, education touchpoints, relationship deepening opportunities, and service escalation protocols. Monitor client experience, retention indicators, and service quality to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and ensure the practice delivers on its client promise. Collaborate with Group Distribution leaders and Field Leaders to identify market opportunities, clarify referral expectations, improve handoff processes, and create consistent field engagement strategies. Create mechanisms for ongoing feedback between Guardian Wealth Partners advisors, Group Distribution and Field partners to improve lead quality, client readiness, and conversion outcomes. Advisor Management & Development Recruit, onboard, coach, and develop a high‑performing team of advisors. Set clear performance expectations, sales goals, and activity metrics aligned with firm objectives. Develop a way to track performance/activity metrics and goals to utilize as coaching and share with senior leadership. Foster a strong sales and advice culture focused on collaboration, professionalism, and continuous improvement. Support advisors through training and coaching in building consultative skills across planning, education, and investment implementation. Required Licenses/Education Series 65/66 Bachelor’s degree Preferred Licenses/Education Advanced degree and/or CFP®, CFA®, or similar credentials preferred Required Experience 10+ years of experience in wealth management, advisory sales, or financial planning, with at least 5 years in a leadership role Deep understanding of fee‑based advisory models, holistic financial planning, and investment management Experience leading advisor teams across multiple client segments, including affluent and HNW Demonstrated experience developing and executing client acquisition, go-to-market, or distribution partnership strategies within wealth management, financial planning, advisory sales, or a related financial services environment. Proven ability to scale sales organizations using digital and hybrid engagement models Strong working knowledge of RIA regulatory and fiduciary standards Proven ability to build and scale servicing and retention models that improve client engagement, deepen relationships, and support long-term business growth. Experience partnering with field distribution, sales leadership, or enterprise channels to build referral strategies, improve lead conversion, and drive practice growth. Strong strategic orientation with the ability to translate business objectives into clear operating plans, performance metrics, advisor routines, and client experience improvements. Job Description: Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Understand and participate across portfolio initiatives, connect dependencies and opportunities across programs to optimize solutions, increase reuse, and reduce data waste. Drive the adoption of a data product operating model across the organization. Champion data product thinking by promoting customer-centric design, product ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable business value. Establish best practices for discoverability, usability, interoperability, governance, and consumption of enterprise data products. Translate business strategy into scalable technology, data, and analytics solutions. Lead discovery workshops and data solution design sessions across underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, reporting, and digital channels. Influence enterprise technology strategy by identifying reusable capabilities and modernization opportunities. Develop reusable frameworks, accelerators, and reference architectures to improve data delivery speed, consistency, and reuse. Design modern data platforms and pipelines that support real-time and batch processing, scalable data integration, and enterprise analytics needs. Ensure high-quality, trusted data through governance, observability, lineage, metadata, and automated data quality controls. Collaborate with data engineering, product, and AI teams to operationalize AI-enabled data solutions within the data ecosystem. Foster collaboration across architecture, engineering, product management, security, data, AI, and business teams. You Have (Required Skills): Deep experience designing and governing enterprise-scale solution architectures across multiple teams and domains. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns. Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems, including application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows. Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level. Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed. Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority. Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction. Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs. Track record of mentoring architects and engineers and elevating organizational capabilities. Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Additional Required Data-Focused Qualifications: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms, data products, or analytics capabilities. Strong understanding of modern data architecture principles, including data mesh, data products, metadata, governance, and domain-driven design. Experience with modern data platforms such as Databricks, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Kafka, or similar technologies. Experience rolling out AI capabilities or AI-enabled solutions within a data ecosystem. Experience within insurance industry, including enrollment, eligibility, policy administration, billing, claims, customer data, and employer administration. Expertise in cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, APIs, microservices, and distributed systems. Strong programming and data engineering skills in Python, PySpark, and SQL. Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills. Experience leading data product initiatives, including proof-of-concept development and feasibility assessment. Familiarity with product management methodologies and Agile frameworks. Success Measures: Increased adoption and reuse of enterprise data products. Improved business outcomes through product-driven data capabilities. Faster delivery of business initiatives through reusable platforms and engineering accelerators. Increased adoption of AI-powered solutions across organization. Higher data quality, trust, discoverability, and governance. Strong cross-functional alignment between business, product, engineering, architecture, and data organizations. Establishment of a sustainable product culture that treats data as a strategic enterprise asset. Job Description: Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Data is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect, Data will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and align to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect, Data focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails, and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. This Principal Solution Architect, Data role will have a strong focus on data solution architecture, modern data platforms, data products, and AI-enabled capabilities across the Insurance business. The role bridges business, engineering, architecture, and data teams to rapidly design, build, and deploy scalable solutions that improve underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, Producer, reporting, analytics, and digital experiences. The architect will champion a data product mindset, treating data as a strategic enterprise asset with clear ownership, quality standards, reusable capabilities, governance, and measurable customer value. Key Responsibilities: Own and shape enterprise or business solution architecture strategy, standards, and patterns across multiple platforms and domains. Define and maintain reference architectures and reusable design patterns (“golden paths”) for solution delivery. Establish architectural guardrails that enable scalable, secure, and consistent solution design across teams. Own reusable solution patterns, reference architectures, golden paths, and cross-team design consistency. Work with Solution Architects to drive adoption; Head of Portfolio Architecture to tailor for BU context; Principal Enterprise Architect to align with enterprise standards. Lead enterprise-level or business-level design decisions for complex, high-impact initiatives that span multiple value streams or business units. Provide architectural oversight and guidance across portfolios, ensuring alignment to enterprise standards and long-term strategy. Drive early engagement on initiatives to identify cross-platform dependencies, systemic risks, and scalability constraints. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and platform teams to define build vs. buy guidance and integration patterns. Translate business and technology strategy into actionable architecture direction and solution designs. Partner with Security, Risk, and Compliance teams to embed governance, security, and regulatory requirements into solution architecture. Define and promote best practices for operational resilience, scalability, performance, and maintainability. Escalate enterprise exceptions, non-standard patterns, and enterprise-risk decisions. Influence and align stakeholders across engineering, product, and business leadership without direct authority. Mentor and coach architects and senior engineers to elevate architectural maturity across the organization. Represent solution architecture in enterprise forums, architecture review boards, and strategic technology discussions. Influence Value Stream leaders, Product Managers, Product Owners, and Tech Leads to align roadmaps, MVP scope, and technical trade-offs. Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Be available for production incidents with major impact to business operations. Understand and participate across portfolio initiatives, connect dependencies and opportunities across programs to optimize solutions, increase reuse, and reduce data waste. Drive the adoption of a data product operating model across the organization. Champion data product thinking by promoting customer-centric design, product ownership, continuous improvement, and measurable business value. Establish best practices for discoverability, usability, interoperability, governance, and consumption of enterprise data products. Translate business strategy into scalable technology, data, and analytics solutions. Lead discovery workshops and data solution design sessions across underwriting, enrollment, billing, claims, customer service, reporting, and digital channels. Influence enterprise technology strategy by identifying reusable capabilities and modernization opportunities. Develop reusable frameworks, accelerators, and reference architectures to improve data delivery speed, consistency, and reuse. Design modern data platforms and pipelines that support real-time and batch processing, scalable data integration, and enterprise analytics needs. Ensure high-quality, trusted data through governance, observability, lineage, metadata, and automated data quality controls. Collaborate with data engineering, product, and AI teams to operationalize AI-enabled data solutions within the data ecosystem. Foster collaboration across architecture, engineering, product management, security, data, AI, and business teams. You Have (Required Qualifications) : Deep experience designing and governing enterprise-scale solution architectures across multiple teams and domains. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven ability to define and drive adoption of architecture standards, frameworks, and reusable patterns. Strong understanding of modern technology ecosystems, including application architectures, APIs and delivery, integration patterns, AI, cloud platforms, and data flows. Experience balancing business priorities, technical trade-offs, and risk at an enterprise level. Demonstrated ability to operate at both strategic and hands-on levels when needed. Strong experience influencing technical direction across distributed teams without direct reporting authority. Ability to bridge business and technology, translating strategy into clear architectural direction. Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience working in regulated or risk-sensitive environments with strong awareness of governance and compliance needs. Track record of mentoring architects and engineers and elevating organizational capabilities. Experience collaborating within Agile / product-based delivery models. Experience producing product-level and team-level technical design documentation. Additional Data-Focused Qualifications Required : Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field. 15+ years of experience in data integration, data architecture, data modeling, data engineering, solution architecture, or enterprise technology. Proven experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale data platforms, data products, or analytics capabilities. Strong understanding of modern data architecture principles, including data mesh, data products, metadata, governance, and domain-driven design. Experience with modern data platforms such as Databricks, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Kafka, or similar technologies. Experience rolling out AI capabilities or AI-enabled solutions within a data ecosystem. Experience within insurance industry, including enrollment, eligibility, policy administration, billing, claims, customer data, and employer administration. Expertise in cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP, APIs, microservices, and distributed systems. Strong programming and data engineering skills in Python, PySpark, and SQL. Exceptional communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills. Experience leading data product initiatives, including proof-of-concept development and feasibility assessment. Familiarity with product management methodologies and Agile frameworks. Success Measures: Increased adoption and reuse of enterprise data products. Improved business outcomes through product-driven data capabilities. Faster delivery of business initiatives through reusable platforms and engineering accelerators. Increased adoption of AI-powered solutions across organization. Higher data quality, trust, discoverability, and governance. Strong cross-functional alignment between business, product, engineering, architecture, and data organizations. Establishment of a sustainable product culture that treats data as a strategic enterprise asset. Location: Three days a week at a Guardian Life Office in Holmdel, NJ, New York, NY or Bethlehem, PA. Job Title: Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform
Job Description: Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform Position Overview: The Principal Solution Architect, Enterprise API Platform, is responsible for defining, scaling, and governing enterprise-wide or business solution architecture across platforms, domains, and delivery teams. This role shapes how technology solutions are designed, integrated, secured, and operated consistently across the organization. While architecture is foundational, the Principal Solution Architect will be responsible for designing solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders.   Where applicable, the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale and algin to business and technology requirements. Operating at an enterprise or portfolio level, the Principal Solution Architect focuses less on individual solution delivery and more on establishing architecture patterns, standards, guardrails and building solutions that enable teams to deliver high-quality, scalable, and secure solutions at speed. This role operates within a federated Enterprise Architecture (EA) model, partnering closely with business technology and platform teams to shape solutions in real time while improving accountability, speed, and delivery alignment. The architect remains connected to the central EA core through enterprise standards, governance, communities of practice, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure consistent, risk-aware technology decisions across domains. This role partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, Product, Cybersecurity, and Platform teams to ensure solutions align to business strategy, are resilient and compliant, and can scale across multiple use cases—without becoming a bottleneck to delivery. For the Enterprise API Platform, this role serves as the strategic and technical architecture partner to the Head of Enterprise API Platform, helping translate API modernization and transformation objectives into practical, value-generating modernization decisions, reusable architecture patterns, MCP-enabled platform direction, and executable engineering outcomes. Proven experience as a Portfolio, Domain, Product or Enterprise Architect in a large, regulated insurance or financial services environment. Deep understanding of insurance operations and systems, including policy administration, underwriting, claims, billing, and distribution. Experience influencing CIO‑level and executive stakeholders on technology strategy and investment decisions. Strong understanding of cloud platforms, modern integration patterns, data platforms, and AI capabilities applied to insurance use cases. Strong ability to simultaneously manage multiple business processes or functions. Exceptional level of accountability, discretion, and independent decision making. Job Title: Head of AI Platform Engineering - Execution Plane
Job Description: As the Head of AI Platform Engineering – Execution Plane, you will lead the development and implementation of our enterprise platform’s execution layer including management of agentic AI workloads, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. You will: You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and technology partners to develop and integrate automation solutions that drive business growth, improve customer experiences, and reduce operational costs. You have: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, engineering, management or a related field. Strong people leadership experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and developing senior technical talent. Deep hands-on technical background designing, building, and operating production-grade distributed systems, AI/ML platforms, data platforms, or cloud-native runtime services. Experience leading teams responsible for the execution layer of a platform, including runtime services, model inference, retrieval, orchestration, tool invocation, workflow execution, or production AI operations. Ability to own the roadmap and delivery for execution plane capabilities such as model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, runtime adapters, MCP services, knowledge bases, retrieval pipelines, inference services, and deployment patterns. Strong understanding of data access patterns, enterprise APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, vector/search systems, context engineering, and governed access to systems of record. Experience building reliable, scalable, low-latency execution services with clear contracts, strong observability, graceful degradation, retry patterns, rate limits, and operational resilience. Ability to partner with control plane, developer experience, data engineering, security, architecture, operations, and domain application teams to ensure execution technologies operate behind governed platform interfaces. Proven ability to drive engineering excellence through design reviews, architecture standards, testing, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, incident response, SLOs, runbooks, and production support mechanisms. Strong understanding of enterprise security and compliance requirements for runtime execution, including identity propagation, auditability, data handling, least privilege access, secrets management, and environment isolation. Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to simplify complex runtime, data, and AI execution topics for senior stakeholders while aligning teams around reusable platform patterns. You will: Experience with agentic AI systems, LLM platforms, model gateways, agent runtimes, tool/action gateways, MCP servers, orchestration frameworks, or AI execution engines. Experience with AWS-based AI execution services and cloud-native patterns, including Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker, Lambda, Step Functions, API Gateway, EKS, DynamoDB, S3, IAM, CloudWatch, and related DevOps tooling. Familiarity with RAG systems, enterprise search, vector databases, embedding models, rerankers, knowledge bases, context engineering, and governed retrieval from enterprise data sources. Experience designing multi-tenant runtime platforms with environment isolation, workload identities, RBAC/ABAC, cross-account access patterns, quotas, throttling, and secure service-to-service communication. Background in MLOps, LLMOps, AIOps, model lifecycle management, evaluation pipelines, model serving, inference optimization, or production AI operations. Experience with observability for AI workloads, including distributed tracing, token usage, latency, model/tool errors, cost attribution, quality metrics, safety metrics, and operational dashboards. Experience with performance, scalability, and cost optimization for high-volume runtime services, including caching, batching, streaming, load testing, capacity planning, and GPU/CPU optimization where applicable. Experience building reusable platform abstractions, SDKs, runtime adapters, reference architectures, or deployment templates that make execution technologies portable across vendors and use cases. Experience integrating enterprise tools, APIs, data services, and workflow systems through governed connectors rather than point-to-point application wiring. Comfort operating in a regulated, matrixed environment where production safety, auditability, resiliency, and vendor optionality are core design principles. Job Description: The Principal Enterprise Architect is a senior architecture leader responsible for shaping, guiding, and advancing enterprise architecture across the organization. Reporting to the Head of Enterprise Architecture and Engineering Enablement , this role translates enterprise strategy into practical architecture direction, standards, target-state designs, and transition roadmaps across business capabilities, applications, platforms, data, integration, cloud, security, and emerging technology domains. While architecture is foundation al, the Principal Enterprise Architect will be responsible for design ing enterprise solutions in close collaboration with the business and technology stakeholders . Where applicable the role will be accountable to build solutions that scale for the enterprise. This position plays a critical role in connecting enterprise strategy to federated execution. The Principal Enterprise Architect partners with architecture, engineering, platform, security, data, and business technology leaders to ensure material technology decisions align with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, modernization priorities, and governance requirements. The role requires strong strategic thinking, architecture breadth, executive communication, and the ability to influence across a large, complex, and federated enterprise environment. The Principal Enterprise Architect provides architecture leadership and recommendations on material technology decisions and has delegated authority within the enterprise architecture operating model as assigned by the Head of Enterprise Architecture. The role is expected to escalate decisions with enterprise-wide impact, non-standard exceptions, or significant risk implications. Key Responsibilities: Enterprise Architecture Leadership Support the Head of Enterprise Architecture in developing and evolving enterprise architecture strategy , principles, standards, and target-state roadmaps. Define and maintain architecture perspectives across business, application, data, integration, cloud, platform, security, and AI-related capabilities as applicable. Own enterprise standards, target state, governance, exceptions, material technology decision frameworks Translate enterprise strategy and target-state direction into practical guidance for domain architecture and engineering teams. Promote alignment across business units, shared services, and technology domains. Strategic Architecture and Transformation Provide architecture leadership for major strategic initiatives, modernization programs, and enterprise-impacting technology decisions. Assess architecture options and recommend solutions that balance business value, cost, risk, resilience, time to market, and long-term maintainability. Support enterprise transformation through simplification, rationalization, modernization, and platform reuse. Identify opportunities to reduce duplication, retire legacy complexity, and improve interoperability across the enterprise. Governance and Decision Support Participate in and support enterprise architecture governance, standards councils, review boards, and strategic decision forums. Evaluate material technology decisions using approved enterprise frameworks, including buy, build, reuse, partner, and retire options. Review architecture proposals for compliance with enterprise standards, target-state architecture, and risk requirements. Support management of architecture exceptions, including rationale, risk analysis, remediation paths, and time-bound approvals. Available for production incidents with major impact to business operations Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with federated domain architects, platform leaders, engineering teams, data and AI teams, security, infrastructure, and business technology leaders to drive alignment. Facilitate resolution of cross-domain design issues, architecture conflicts, and overlapping capability decisions. Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across technology and business-aligned delivery organizations. Ensure architecture direction is understood and applied consistently across federated teams. Works with Business Unit heads and principal solution architects to translate enterprise direction into federated execution. Risk, Security, and Resilience Incorporate cybersecurity, privacy, resilience, recoverability, and regulatory considerations into architecture guidance and recommendations. Partner with risk, security, and compliance stakeholders to ensure technology decisions align with enterprise control requirements. Assess the operational and architectural implications of technology choices in regulated and high-availability environments. Talent and Capability Development Mentor and coach architects and senior technology professionals. Contribute to architecture capability development, communities of practice, and architecture operating model maturity. Support common role expectations, competency models, and quality standards across the architecture function. Promote enterprise-first thinking, sound decision-making, and strong architecture discipline. You Have: Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science , Information Systems, Engineering, or related field. 1 2 + years of progressive experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture, domain architecture, or senior technology strategy roles. Deep cross-domain expertise spanning applications, integration, data, AI, cloud, security, and platform strategy. Experience supporting or leading architecture for large-scale transformation initiatives in complex enterprise environments. Experience with architecture governance, standards development, target-state planning, and strategic technology decision-making. Proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority. Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills. Preferred Education and Experience Experience in insurance, financial services, healthcare, or another highly regulated industry. Experience in a federated technology organization with centralized architecture direction and distributed execution. Experience with cloud modernization, API strategies, platform engineering, data ecosystems, and enterprise integration. Familiarity with AI-enabled enterprise capabilities, automation, and emerging technology trends. Advanced degree and/or relevant certifications such as TOGAF, SAFe , AWS, Azure, GCP, or equivalent. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Strong knowledge of enterprise architecture principles, methods, and governance practices. Broad understanding of enterprise technology domains and cross-domain dependencies. Ability to develop target-state architecture and pragmatic transition approaches. Strong business acumen and ability to connect architecture decisions to business outcomes. Ability to assess tradeoffs among speed, cost, quality, risk, and strategic fit. Strong facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to communicate effectively with executive, business, and technical audiences. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity and lead through influence. Job Description: The Enterprise Data Solutions & Operations (EDSO) team within the Digital & Technology (D-T) function is looking to staff a Head of Data Solutions (the ‘Role’) for our FPRS/CSWM line of business. This role will work closely with core FPRS/CSWM business value streams (e.g., distribution mgmt., shop, purchasing, service, claims, etc.) to define, shape, prioritize and lead the delivery and evolution of key data and information product (‘Products’) solutions supporting business objectives. More specifically, this role will drive the capture and planning for new demand of features and/or enhancements to Guardian’s data Products as articulated by key business leaders from one or more key value stream and/or the respective FPRS/CSWM FP&A functional BI leader. These data Products include everything from consumer-facing analytics (reports/dashboards), to inter/intra-application data services (APIs/extracts/shares), to data services supporting AI/GenAI automation, to the underlying data definitions and reference data that define the FPRS/CSWM businesses. In addition, this role will have accountability for planning and delivering strategic data initiatives within one or more FPRS/CSWM value stream, collaborating with the value stream Digital & Tech (D&T) Leader, the value stream Business Leader, the value stream Product Delivery Managers (PDMs), and the value stream Product Owners(POs)) to identify/scope/size and execute key data needs, and to identify and raise new opportunities for data activation/adoption. A key aspect of the role will be to balance the needs across value stream demands, soliciting/recommending priorities, and in turn, incorporating and aligning these priorities into a roadmap and plan for delivery, including resource planning (business SMEs, UAT participants, etc.), training, and activation in support of full value realization. Finally, the FPRS/CSWM Data Solution Head will direct the data steward(s) in their charter to continuously capture metadata related to all data elements (e.g., definition, quality standards, calculation logic, SLA requirements, etc.), and to report/coordinate any data quality issues/SLA breaches/definitional changes to the same. From a strategic management perspective, the role will bring a keen understanding of value stream processes, supporting applications and key data elements. Moreover, the role will establish and nurture relationships with both value stream executive leadership, as well as functional and analytic SMEs in the value stream teams to keep a pulse on the latent needs and direction of the business. Using these relationships, the role will anticipate future data needs, constantly updating and communicating the backlog of features to be addressed in the data/info product roadmap - all in close coordination with business partners in the FPRS/CSWM FP&A analytics team(s). From an org management perspective, the Role will directly manage and grow a team of data product owners (DPOs).  These DPOs will be aligned with FPRS/CSWM value stream data products and will drive the execution of new build features/enhancements to their respective data products. In addition, the Role will manage both direct (EDSO FPRS/CSWM Solution Engineering team members, EDSO FPRS/CSWM Data Product Owners) and indirect (D&T Solution & Data Architecture resources, and D&T Data Governance resources), in order to drive the successful delivery of data products, as well as to help foster the development of the next generation of D&T data leaders, You are: You are a highly independent senior manager with the ability to (or rapidly become) conversant in life insurance and wealth management products and their respective business processes. You have an aptitude for using and shaping data solutions in support of business objectives and are able to clearly articulate the value that can be attributable to data/info products. You are highly organized, staying abreast of multiple stakeholders’ priorities, the status of multiple parallel initiatives/projects/data products, and the state of value realization and adoption for production data assets. You communicate fluidly and extemporaneously, able to articulate how data solution functionality will meet business needs in a brief, non-technical manner. While you may not be a recent ‘hands on keyboards’ technologist (you may even have come from a business or analytical background), you have a deep understanding of data and analytic technologies, architectural principles, and you aren’t afraid to dig into data models and pipeline logic. Finally, you are reliable in terms of your commitments, honest and brave with issues/escalations, and have a client service mentality. You have: 15+ years of experience with an escalating competency in data and analytic solutions BS or BA required; MS or MBA preferred 3+ years working in an agile environment 3+ years of experience managing staff/teams, potentially (preferably) with geographically diverse teams, often organized on a product delivery basis (highly matrixed) 5+ years of experience with standard program management tools (such as JIRA, AgileCraft, ATIIM, etc.), as well as desktop collaboration/ideation tools (Sharepoint, MSOffice, OneDrive, Lucid, Draw.io, etc.) Experience in life insurance and wealth management products and industry preferred (e.g., whole/term/universal/supplemental/etc., as well as , FIA, portfolio/client management tools for FAs/Brokers, etc.) Experience with enterprise data management principles such as data ownership/stewardship (experience as a data domain steward or data product owner would be a plus) Ability to document and capture business requirements in detail, including metric calculation logic, quality/timeliness expectations, analytic functionality, hierarchies, etc., as well as functional user journeys as they relate to data solutions A client focus with strong verbal and written communication skills, able to manage multiple stakeholders and creatively align their interests, and able to lead workshops on ideation/requirements with little preparation Strong organizational and time management skills; ability to multi-task and driving teams to meet aggressive delivery commitments Proactive problem-solving and information research skills Ability to manage/mentor earlier tenure and/or less experienced staff to help grow future leaders and deepen value stream knowledge on the broader team Ability to accept change in stride, remaining flexible due to changing business needs/priorities Natural ‘teacher’, able to coach business partners on optimal use of data assets to meet stated/latent business needs Comfort with/knowledge of analytic tools This role is responsible for driving strategic transformation initiatives across the Finance organization to improve performance, optimize processes, advance AI-enabled capabilities, and strengthen data-driven decision-making. Reporting to the Head of Finance & Risk Transformation, Strategy and Operations, s/he will partner closely with Finance, Technology, Risk, Operations, Data, and business leaders to design and implement future-state operating models, modernize planning and reporting processes, and deliver sustainable business value. You will Key Responsibilities Transformation Strategy & Execution Develop and execute Finance transformation strategies aligned with business and enterprise objectives. Lead large-scale transformation initiatives spanning Finance processes, operating models, systems, data, controls, and organizational capabilities. Manage transformation roadmaps, implementation plans, milestones, dependencies, and value realization objectives. Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, effectiveness, decision support, governance, and stakeholder experience. Drive continuous improvement and innovation across Finance functions. AI Enablement & Digital Innovation Lead the Finance AI strategy and roadmap, identifying opportunities to leverage Generative AI, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and agentic AI solutions to improve productivity, decision-making, and business outcomes. Partner with Finance leaders to identify, prioritize, and scale high-value AI use cases across FP&A, forecasting, management reporting, expense management, financial close, workforce planning, and decision support. Drive adoption of enterprise AI capabilities, including Microsoft Copilot, Claude, AI agents, and emerging technologies, ensuring alignment with business priorities and governance expectations. Support transformation initiatives involving ERP modernization, Oracle Planning/EPM, enterprise performance management, reporting platforms, AI-enabled workflows, and automation solutions. Strong understanding of Finance operating models, planning, forecasting, reporting, expense management, and performance management processes. Experience developing transformation roadmaps, business cases, benefits realization plans, and executive-level presentations. Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence senior stakeholders across business, technology, data, risk, and operations. Strong analytical, facilitation, problem-solving, communication, and executive storytelling skills. Experience within Financial Services, Insurance, Banking, Risk Management, or other highly regulated industries. Experience implementing Oracle Planning, Oracle EPM Cloud, Hyperion, SAP, Workday, Anaplan, or similar Finance platforms. Job Description: As a Senior Product Owner, Wealth Management, you will be responsible for defining, prioritizing, and driving product capabilities that support the Wealth Management business and enable a more intuitive, efficient, and valuable experience. This role serves as a critical connection point between business strategy, field/advisor needs, operational processes, technology delivery, data capabilities, and third-party platform partners. This role requires strong product ownership discipline, deep collaboration skills, and the ability to balance competing stakeholder needs while helping drive alignment, priorities, decisions, and execution. You will Translate product vision and business strategy into a prioritized backlog, clear requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and delivery priorities aligned to business, customer, and enterprise goals. Partner with Product Managers, Technology Leads, business stakeholders, operations, data, compliance, and third-party providers to deliver Wealth Management capabilities that create business value and improve user experience. Build deep understanding of Wealth Management workflows, products, services, processes, data needs, advisor experience gaps, operational challenges, and technology dependencies to shape product decisions and improvement opportunities. Define, prioritize, sequence, and refine enhancements, integrations, process improvements and actionable backlog items with the Product Manager and Technology Lead. Collaborate with technology, vendor, data, analytics, and AI partners to support reporting needs, governance expectations, and data/AI standards into product solutions. Use process analysis, root cause analysis, and stakeholder feedback to identify opportunities across advisor, client, operations, and business user experiences. Support release readiness, communications, training needs, adoption planning, feedback loops, OKR tracking, milestone reporting, and stakeholder updates to maintain delivery momentum and business alignment. Required Experience: A minimum of 5–7 years of experience in product management, product ownership, business transformation, technology delivery, or a related field. Experience working in or supporting the wealth management industry Familiarity with wealth management platforms, financial planning platforms, portfolio management tools, or other wealth management technology solutions. Knowledge of wealth management products, advisor/client workflows, operations, and business processes, Proven experience translating business needs, customer research, stakeholder feedback, and strategic priorities into roadmaps, requirements, user stories, and delivery plans. Experience working with cross-functional teams with the ability to collaborate effectively with multiple stakeholders while helping drive toward clear priorities, informed decisions, and timely execution. Strong product ownership skills, including backlog management, prioritization, acceptance criteria development, dependency management, and release readiness. Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to clearly explain complex concepts to both business and technical audiences. Preferred Experience Understanding of RIAs or broker-dealer operations, and investment products. Understanding of the advisor experience, including how advisors engage with clients, manage relationships, complete business processes, access data, and use technology to support growth and service. Job Description: The Objective of the Underwriting Consultant, Large Market will be to work with Sales, Underwriting, Products and Pricing areas to profitably grow Guardian's Large Market revenue and market share in the 1,000 lives and over market space. Key objectives will be to achieve targeted sales and earnings goals, train, and mentor less experienced underwriters, manage complex technical underwriting issues, train account management, handle projects and recommend policy and strategy changes. The Underwriting Consultant is responsible for to provide pricing and plan design for companies with 1,000 or more lives utilizing prior claim experience and manual rates. Products include Group Dental, Vision, FMLA, STD, LTD, and Life insurance. The underwriter will be an excellent negotiator who builds collaborative relationships with Sales and other areas of Guardian to solve business issues and win. The underwriter will be both a confident communicator and an independent decision-maker. You are A leader who will exhibit Guardian's Ways of Working: Think Big and Grow, Accelerate Impact, and Lead Change One who continuously strives to provide superior products and customer service Accountable and willing to take ownership for meeting individual performance objectives Ethical - you will uphold Guardians commitment to ethical business practices and lead by example You will Recommend competitively priced products, funding arrangements, and services to meet customer requirements Determine pricing of new business and/or renewal business, including alternate plan of benefit options Communicate rate/fee development and plan design offered. Assess contract comparisons for takeover business Negotiate with sales representatives or agents/brokers to resolve rate questions and risk related concerns Manage administrative processing of cases. Utilize underwriting systems and databases for quotes, sales, renewals to track results Document case decisions and underwriting rationale Provide mentoring/coaching to help develop technical skills of others, support team growth, and development initiatives Conduct training for sales and/or underwriting staff as needed Participate in project work or on teams to develop or improve underwriting processes. Responsible for oversight and identification of any barriers to achievement of financial goals. Produce solutions that lead to target result achievement Improve Guardian's underwriting strategies to support key growth goals and to assume an industry leadership position in the 1,000+ employer marketplace Have the opportunity to enhance the overall talent and knowledge level of Large Market Underwriting, Sales, and Account Management Be a go to person for technical issues and decision making for other team members Advise others on how to handle irregular administrative requests or technical underwriting risk analysis based not only on experience, but also as capacity as a leader Be a go to person for the Regional Underwriting Leader for the most complex work or key project work Handle a delegated part of a larger task for completion and integration with the overall deliverable In addition to being a participant on a project, be a leader within a project team or process team who defines, organizes, and directs tasks that need to get done Help support Large Market team management with activities that are key drivers for the team to achieve results Continuously evaluate underwriting strategies, guidelines, and pricing relative to Guardian's internal results and external competitive position Recommend policy strategy changes. Job Title: NY Site and Executive Support Lead
Job Description: Guardian is seeking a NY Site and Executive Support Lead to join the Digital Workplace organization. This role serves as the primary technology leader for the New York and Stamford offices while delivering high-touch, white-glove support to senior executives and their administrative teams. The position combines hands-on executive support with site ownership, ensuring a consistent, high-quality workplace technology experience across locations. The individual will act as a trusted partner to business leadership, owning the end-to-end support experience, driving service performance, and ensuring seamless execution during high-visibility and time-sensitive situations. This role requires strong technical expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to operate calmly under pressure while maintaining the highest level of professionalism, discretion, and accountability. This role supports senior leaders and enterprise meetings where reliability, security, professionalism, and discretion are essential. You Will : Executive and End User Support Provide high touch technology support for senior executives, including devices, collaboration tools, and audiovisual environments. Act as an escalation point for complex or high impact executive support issues. Support leadership meetings, town halls, and enterprise events, including live troubleshooting during sessions when needed. End User Computing and Device Management Support and troubleshoot Windows endpoints and virtual desktop solutions, including Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, AWS Workspaces, and traditional VDI platforms. Maintain hands on working knowledge of Microsoft Intune, SCCM, and Windows Autopilot. Manage executive device lifecycle activities such as provisioning, ongoing maintenance, refresh, and retirement. Audiovisual and Collaboration Support Provide on site and remote support for executive conference rooms, meeting spaces, and hybrid work environments. Support Microsoft Teams Rooms and associated audiovisual hardware, including cameras, microphones, displays, and room control systems. Partner with Facilities, vendors, and event stakeholders to ensure meetings are properly prepared and executed. Security and Compliance Ensure executive support practices align with Guardian policies, security standards, and regulatory requirements. Work closely with Security and Infrastructure teams to maintain secure configurations and protect sensitive executive data. Handle business critical and executive issues with appropriate confidentiality and professionalism. Innovation, Automation, and AI Maintain a working understanding of AI and GenAI technologies relevant to digital workplace operations. Identify opportunities to improve user experience through automation and process improvement. Support the adoption of modern tools and capabilities aligned with Guardian’s Digital Workplace strategy. Collaboration and Vendor Management Collaborate with cross functional partners including Security, Infrastructure, HR, Real Estate, and business teams. Manage relationships with AV and technology vendors and contribute to evaluations of new solutions. Document standards, procedures, and operational practices as needed. You Are : This role requires a self starter who is highly accountable and comfortable working independently as well as part of a team. The individual must be able to operate effectively in fast paced, high visibility environments and make sound decisions under pressure. Strong troubleshooting skills, clear communication, and comfort interacting with senior leadership are essential. The ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality and attention to detail is required. Experience working within executive or VIP support models. Background in incident and escalation management in enterprise IT environments. Experience developing operational documentation and runbooks. Prior experience mentoring support staff or serving as a senior technical lead. Proactive planning and readiness support for executive meetings and events. You Have : Ten or more years of IT experience with at least five years focused on digital workplace, end user computing, or executive support. Demonstrated experience supporting senior executives or other high visibility business users. Strong experience with the Microsoft 365 ecosystem including Intune, SCCM, and Autopilot. Hands on experience with virtual desktop platforms such as Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, and AWS Workspaces. Familiarity with Microsoft E5 Security capabilities, device lifecycle management, automation, and enterprise audiovisual and collaboration environments. Location Hybrid 3 days onsite. Hudson Yards in New York City, This role requires travel to other Guardian locations including Holmdel, NJ, Bethlehem Pennsylvania, and additional sites as needed. Job Description: As the Head of Platform Engineering – Control Plane, you will lead the development and implementation of our platform control plane initiatives which include governance layer as a code and all control functions directing our execution plan. Your role is pivotal in building and scaling a highly flexible, scalable, governed execution plane. You will: You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, stakeholders, and technology partners to develop and integrate automation solutions that drive business growth, improve customer experiences, and reduce operational costs. You have: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, engineering, management or a related field. Strong people leadership experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and developing senior technical talent. Deep hands-on technical background designing, building, and operating distributed, cloud-native platform services in production. Experience leading platform, infrastructure, developer platform, AI/ML platform, security platform, or other reusable enterprise engineering capabilities. Ability to own the roadmap and delivery for control plane capabilities such as identity and access management, tenant boundaries, policy enforcement, approvals, evaluation gates, observability, auditability, FinOps, secrets management, and lifecycle/promotion workflows. Strong understanding of enterprise governance, security, risk, compliance, and operational controls required to safely run AI or data-intensive systems in production. Experience building reliable APIs, registries, workflow services, policy engines, or orchestration services with clear contracts for downstream engineering teams. Proven ability to drive engineering excellence through architecture reviews, design standards, testing, CI/CD, observability, incident response, reliability practices, and operational metrics. Ability to partner effectively with product, architecture, security, risk, compliance, operations, and domain engineering teams to turn ambiguous platform needs into scalable engineering outcomes. Strong communication and influence skills, with the ability to simplify complex technical topics for senior stakeholders and align teams around platform standards. High ownership mindset with a bias for durable, reusable platform capabilities over one-off solutions. You will: Experience with agentic AI systems, LLM platforms, model gateways, tool/action gateways, agent registries, evaluation frameworks, or AI developer tooling. Familiarity with AI governance patterns such as prompt-injection defense, PII handling, output filtering, risk tiering, model/tool allow-lists, HITL controls, and audit trails. Experience with AWS-based platform engineering, including services such as Bedrock, SageMaker, Lambda, DynamoDB, API Gateway, EKS, IAM, CloudWatch, and related DevOps tooling. Experience designing or operating multi-tenant platforms with RBAC/ABAC, entitlement models, service accounts, policy-as-code, and secure cross-account or cross-environment access patterns. Knowledge of observability, tracing, telemetry, cost attribution, and platform-level operational dashboards for enterprise-scale systems. Experience establishing developer-friendly paved roads, reference architectures, templates, SDKs, CLI tools, or self-service workflows that improve adoption and reduce support burden. Experience working in regulated environments where security, compliance, data residency, retention, and auditability are first-class platform requirements. Background in MLOps, LLMOps, AIOps, model lifecycle management, or production AI operations. Experience with vendor integration strategies that preserve portability and avoid lock-in through stable platform interfaces and clear architectural contracts. Comfort operating in a matrixed, global organization with onshore/offshore teams, multiple stakeholders, and evolving platform priorities. Job Description: The Senior IAM Engineer will be responsible for designing, implementing, and handling identity and access management (IAM) solutions to ensure the security and efficiency of the organization's IT infrastructure. This role involves working closely with various groups to understand their IAM needs and providing expert guidance on standard methodologies and solutions. You Will: Design and implement IAM solutions, including identity governance, access management, and privileged access management. Develop and maintain IAM policies, procedures, and standards to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry best practices. Collaborate with IT and security teams to integrate IAM solutions with existing systems and applications. Conduct regular audits and assessments of IAM systems to identify and mitigate potential security risks. Provide technical support and troubleshooting for IAM-related issues. Stay up to date with the latest trends and technologies in IAM and recommend improvements to existing systems and processes. Mentor and provide guidance to junior IAM engineers and other team members. You Have: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or a related field. At least 5 years of experience in IAM engineering or a related field. Strong knowledge of IAM concepts, technologies, and standard processes. Experience with IAM platforms, including Okta, PingFederate, SailPoint, CyberArk, and Microsoft Azure AD/Entra ID. Experience with reverse proxy solutions, including Okta Access Gateway and Microsoft App Proxy. Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Good communication and interpersonal skills. Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or similar are a plus. Passion for problem-solving and continuous curiosity to learn. Understanding of security control concepts and their application in IAM. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Strong organizational and time management skills. You Are: Experience with cloud-based IAM solutions and integrations. Knowledge of regulatory requirements and standards related to IAM, such as GDPR, HIPAA, and SOX. Experience with DevOps, CI/CD, and AWS. Experience with scripting and automation tools to streamline IAM processes. Job Description: Role Purpose Lead the execution of Guardian’s AI governance program by operationalizing enterprise policies, standards, and guardrails across AI models, copilots, agents, and RAG ‑ based workflows. This role ensures AI governance is consistently implemented, scalable, and embedded into delivery and platform workflows—enabling responsible AI adoption while managing risk. The AI Governance Lead partners closely with Data Science, AI Platforms, Data Management, Data Governance, Risk, Legal, and Technology teams to translate enterprise AI governance strategy into practical processes, controls, and day ‑ to ‑ day ways of working. Responsibilities AI Governance Execution & Program Leadership Lead the execution of Guardian’s AI governance program across analytics, AI, and agentic use cases. Implement enterprise AI governance policies, standards, and guardrails in alignment with defined risk appetite and regulatory expectations. Ensure governance processes are repeatable, risk ‑ based , and scalable—not bespoke or ad hoc. Operating Model & Workflow Integration Own the AI governance operating model, including intake, review, escalation, monitoring, and change management processes. Govern AI model lifecycles and AI system behaviors across models, copilots, agents, and RAG workflows, including retrieval strategies, tool use, actions, and human ‑ in ‑ the ‑ loop requirements. Embed AI governance controls into platforms and delivery workflows so controls are observable, durable, and auditable. Standards, Controls & Risk Management Operationalize governance standards for AI development, deployment, monitoring, and retirement. Implement risk ‑ based controls and escalation paths based on use case type, data sensitivity, and impact. Partner with Risk, Legal, Compliance, and Security teams to ensure AI governance execution meets internal and external requirements. Cross ‑ Functional Partnership Serve as the primary AI governance partner to data science, analytics, engineering, and product teams. Coordinate with Data Management and Data Governance leaders to ensure AI governance aligns with data controls, quality expectations, and AI ‑ readiness requirements. Support enterprise governance forums by preparing materials, surfacing risks, and enabling timely decision ‑ making . Measurement & Continuous Improvement Define and track operational KPIs for AI governance execution, including coverage, exceptions, monitoring effectiveness, and remediation trends. Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and emerging risks; recommend adjustments to processes, controls, and tooling. Continuously improve governance mechanisms as AI capabilities and use cases evolve. Leadership & Influence Provide leadership to AI governance practitioners and analysts; set priorities, manage workload, and build governance expertise . Influence senior stakeholders across business, technology, and risk through strong execution, transparency, and practical problem ‑ solving . Requirements - 12+ years of experience in data, analytics, AI, technology risk, or related disciplines. - Demonstrated experience governing AI systems, including models and agentic workflows, at enterprise scale. - Strong understanding of AI lifecycle considerations, data usage patterns, and risk management principles. - Proven ability to develop and tr anslate strategy into executable standards, workflows, and operating models. - Experience influencing senior stakeholders across business, technology, risk, and legal teams. - Excellent communication skills and ability to operate through influence rather than direct control. Job Summary Guardian is seeking a highly capable AV Support Engineer to join the Digital Workplace organization. This role is responsible for delivering reliable, high-touch audiovisual and collaboration support across conference rooms, executive meeting spaces, and enterprise event environments. This is a hands-on, customer-facing role supporting Microsoft Teams Rooms and modern hybrid collaboration technologies. The position requires strong technical depth, composure under pressure, and the ability to resolve issues in real time during business-critical meetings and events. The ideal candidate operates independently, partners effectively across IT, Facilities, and vendors, and takes ownership of delivering a consistent, high-quality meeting experience across all locations. Key Responsibilities AV and Collaboration Support Provide onsite and remote support for conference rooms, boardrooms, training rooms, and hybrid collaboration spaces Support Microsoft Teams Rooms and related AV technologies including cameras, microphones, DSPs, displays, and control systems Perform real-time troubleshooting during live meetings, minimizing disruption and ensuring a seamless experience Conduct pre-meeting room validation checks to ensure readiness and reliability Event and Executive Support Deliver white-glove support for executive meetings, town halls, and enterprise events Manage end-to-end AV support including setup, testing, live operation, and teardown Partner with business stakeholders and event organizers to define requirements and ensure successful execution Support live and hybrid events including streaming, recording, and broadcast workflows End User Support and Experience Support collaboration tools including Microsoft Teams and related conferencing platforms Provide direct assistance to end users, including executives, ensuring a high-quality and consistent meeting experience Deliver basic user guidance and training on AV and meeting technologies AV Operations and Reliability Perform routine health checks, preventative maintenance, and system validation across AV-enabled spaces Monitor and troubleshoot recurring issues; perform root cause analysis and recommend long-term fixes Maintain high availability and performance of AV systems aligned to business expectations Track incidents, resolutions, and trends to improve service quality and reduce repeat issues Engineering Collaboration and Standards Partner with engineering teams to standardize room designs, configurations, and support models Assist with AV deployments, upgrades, and lifecycle management across sites Review vendor installations to ensure alignment with enterprise standards and quality expectations Create and maintain documentation including room standards, SOPs, and troubleshooting guides Vendor and Stakeholder Management Act as a key point of contact for AV vendors, integrators, and service providers Coordinate installations, repairs, and maintenance activities Work closely with Facilities and Real Estate teams to support workspace technology initiatives Security and Compliance Ensure AV and collaboration technologies align with enterprise security and compliance requirements Partner with Security and Infrastructure teams to maintain secure configurations Support audit and risk management activities as needed Continuous Improvement and Innovation Identify opportunities to improve the user experience, system reliability, and operational efficiency Recommend enhancements through automation, monitoring, and standardization Stay current on emerging AV, collaboration, and hybrid workplace technologies Qualifications Experience 8–10 years of IT experience, with at least 5 years focused on AV, video conferencing Proven experience supporting enterprise conference rooms, collaboration environments, and live events Experience in multi-site or campus environments strongly preferred Technical Skills Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Teams Rooms and enterprise collaboration platforms Deep knowledge of AV hardware including cameras, microphones, speakers, displays, and control systems Understanding of AV signal flow, cabling, and AV-over-IP concepts Experience troubleshooting integrated AV/IT environments and network-connected systems Familiarity with AV management, monitoring, and asset tracking tools Professional Skills Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, especially under time pressure during live events Ability to operate independently and manage multiple priorities in fast-paced environments Excellent communication skills with the ability to support both technical and non-technical stakeholders Customer-focused mindset with an emphasis on delivering a high-quality user experience High attention to detail and accountability for outcomes Additional Preferred Skills Experience supporting large-scale AV environments across multiple locations Exposure to incident management, escalation handling, and IT service management frameworks Experience documenting standards, runbooks, and operational procedures Background in hybrid meeting support, live event production, or streaming technologies Relevant certifications such as AVIXA CTS or vendor-specific AV certifications preferred but not required Why This Role Matters This role sits at the intersection of technology and user experience. You will directly impact how employees collaborate, communicate, and engage—particularly in high-visibility meetings where reliability and professionalism are critical. Modern AV environments are tightly integrated with enterprise IT systems, requiring a blend of AV expertise, networking knowledge, and customer-centric execution. Job Title: Workday Technical Lead, Payroll, Time & Absence
Job Description: Position Summary The Workday Technical Lead – Payroll, Time & Absence is responsible for the end-to-end technical ownership, design, and governance of Workday Payroll, Time Tracking, and Absence modules. This role serves as the system authority for the domain, ensuring scalable design, data integrity, and alignment with business and compliance requirements. This position operates within IT and partners closely with Payroll, HR, and external vendors to deliver reliable, efficient, and compliant solutions.
